chapters.title: Chapter 1: What Makes a Stock Cyclical or Defensive

lessons.title: The Spectrum: Deep Cyclicals, Early Cyclicals, Quasi-Defensives, and True Defensives

body.text: Cyclical and defensive are not two boxes. They are two ends of a line, and most of the money in your portfolio sits somewhere in the middle. Knowing exactly where tells you how hard each holding will get hit, and when.

children.text: In the last lesson you learned the test: what happens to profits when the economy slows. Apply that test across the whole NSE and you will not get two neat groups. You will get steel companies whose profits vanish, banks whose profits dip and recover, IT firms whose growth stalls but whose profits barely move, and soap makers who hardly notice. This lesson maps that range into five positions you can actually use.

cells: Deep cyclical
Profits collapse, losses are common at the trough
Global commodity prices and capacity
Tata Steel, JSW Steel, Hindalco, Vedanta, NMDC
Early cyclical
Profits fall sharply but recover first when rates ease
Interest rates, credit availability, consumer confidence
Maruti Suzuki, Bajaj Auto, DLF, SBI, Bajaj Finance
Late cyclical
Profits hold for a while on existing orders, then fall, and recover last
Corporate and government capex
L&T, Siemens, ABB India, BHEL, UltraTech Cement
Quasi-defensive
Growth slows noticeably, but profits rarely fall much
Global client budgets, regulation, pricing cycles
TCS, Infosys, Sun Pharma, Bharti Airtel, Apollo Hospitals
True defensive
Profits keep growing or dip only slightly
Everyday necessity demand or regulated returns
Hindustan Unilever, Nestle India, Colgate-Palmolive India, Power Grid

body.title: Illustrative Worst-Year Profit Change in a Typical Slowdown

children.text: These bars are illustrative, not averages from a dataset. Real numbers vary by cycle and by company. What holds is the ordering: the further left a business sits, the deeper its worst year tends to be.
Deep Cyclicals: Price Takers on a Global Market

markDefs.definition: A company that cannot set its own selling price and must accept whatever the market price is, typically because its product is a standardised commodity.

children.text: Steel, aluminium, zinc, iron ore, and commodity chemicals are the same product whoever makes them. That makes these companies

. When China's construction slows or global capacity outruns demand, prices fall for everyone, and a Tata Steel or Vedanta cannot do anything about it. Add huge fixed costs from blast furnaces, smelters, and debt, and profits do not just dip. They disappear. These are the most volatile earnings on the NSE.
Early vs Late Cyclicals: Same Cycle, Different Timing

Not all cyclicals turn at the same time. Some respond almost immediately when the RBI cuts rates and loans get cheaper. Others only see demand months or years later, once companies are confident enough to build new factories. Holding both is not the same as being diversified, because they are riding the same wave at different points.

columns.label: Early cyclicals
points: Demand depends on EMIs and consumer confidence
Respond quickly to RBI rate cuts and easier credit
Monthly data shows the turn early: auto sales, housing sales, loan growth
Examples: two-wheelers and cars, housing developers, banks and NBFCs, consumer durables

columns.label: Late cyclicals
points: Demand depends on companies and the government committing to capex
Capex happens only once existing capacity is nearly full
Order books cushion the downturn at first, then run dry
Examples: capital goods, engineering and construction, power equipment, industrial cement demand

body.title: How a Typical Indian Upcycle Travels Through the Spectrum

events.title: RBI eases
events.description: Inflation cools, the RBI cuts the repo rate, and banks start passing on lower lending rates.

events.title: Early cyclicals pick up
events.description: Home loan and auto loan EMIs fall. Car, two-wheeler, and housing sales improve. Bank and NBFC loan growth accelerates.

events.title: Capacity fills up
events.description: Rising demand pushes factory capacity utilisation higher. Companies start planning expansions.

events.title: Late cyclicals win orders
events.description: Capex announcements turn into orders for L&T, Siemens, ABB India, and cement makers. Their revenues rise for years on the back of these order books.

events.title: Commodities peak
events.description: Construction and manufacturing demand is at its height. Steel and metal prices and profits are near their highs, just before the cycle turns.

body.text: This sequence is a tendency, not a timetable. Global commodity prices can move deep cyclicals regardless of where India is in its own cycle, and government infrastructure spending can support late cyclicals even when private capex is weak. Chapter 5 shows how to track where the cycle actually is.

markDefs.definition: The provisions a bank sets aside for loans that may not be repaid, expressed as a cost against its profit.

children.text: Banks are early cyclicals on the way up, because loan growth responds quickly to lower rates and better confidence. On the way down, their pain shows up with a lag through

: loans given during the boom turn bad a few years later. India's corporate bad loan cycle is the clearest example. Loans made to steel, power, and infrastructure companies during the 2008 to 2012 capex boom turned into non-performing assets, and State Bank of India reported a net loss for FY18 as it provided for them. So banks are cyclical, but their earnings cycle is set by the credit cycle as much as by GDP.
Quasi-Defensives: Growth Is Cyclical, Profits Are Not

This middle group trips up the most investors. Indian IT services is the best example. When US and European clients cut technology budgets, revenue growth at TCS and Infosys slows sharply, as it did in FY24 when growth fell to low single digits. But these companies have almost no debt, flexible employee costs, and long client contracts, so profits slow rather than collapse. The stock can still fall hard on slower growth, but the earnings do not behave like steel. Pharma, telecom, and hospitals sit here too, each with its own risk: USFDA actions for pharma, tariff decisions for telecom, and regulation for hospitals.

body.title: The Quasi-Defensive Pattern
body.textWithBlank: For a quasi-defensive business, a slowdown mainly hits revenue ___ rather than causing absolute profits to collapse.
body.explanation: Quasi-defensives keep earning profits in a downturn, but the pace at which revenue and profit grow slows noticeably. That slower growth can still hurt the share price, especially if the stock was priced for fast growth.

children.text: True defensives earn their place in one of two ways. Staples companies like Hindustan Unilever, Nestle India, and Colgate-Palmolive India sell low-ticket products bought every week, backed by brands strong enough to pass on cost increases. Regulated utilities like Power Grid earn returns on their assets that are set by a regulator, not by how much electricity the economy consumes this year. In a slowdown, the worst a true defensive usually sees is slower volume growth, as households shift to smaller packs or cheaper variants.

body.title: Place the Company
body.question: A company builds metro rail systems, power plants, and refineries. Its order book covers about three years of revenue. Where does it most likely sit on the spectrum?
body.explanation: Its demand comes from government and corporate capex, which picks up late in the cycle. The multi-year order book keeps revenue flowing for a while after the economy slows, then new orders dry up. That delayed pattern is typical of a late cyclical like L&T.

children.text: Map Your Mutual Fund Onto the Spectrum

Every equity fund factsheet lists its sector allocation. Below is an illustrative large-cap fund. Most investors would call it diversified because it holds ten sectors. Group those sectors by spectrum position and a different picture appears.

body.title: How Cyclical Is This Fund?
body.prompt: Using the spectrum from this lesson, add up the fund's allocation to deep, early, and late cyclicals combined: banks and financials, capital goods, autos, and metals. What percentage of the fund is cyclical?
body.explanation: Banks and financials 30 + autos 8 (early cyclicals) + capital goods 10 (late cyclical) + metals 5 (deep cyclical) = 53%. Quasi-defensives (IT 15, pharma 7, telecom 5) make up 27%, and true defensives (FMCG 10, power utilities 5) only 15%. Ten sectors, but more than half the fund rides the economic cycle.

body.title: The Salaried Investor's Blind Spot
body.scenario: Karan works in sales at a commercial vehicle manufacturer in Pune. His direct equity portfolio on Zerodha holds Tata Motors, Bajaj Finance, L&T, JSW Steel, and HDFC Bank. He says he is well diversified: five companies across five different sectors.
body.prompt: Is Karan as diversified as he thinks? What would you point out?
body.modelAnswer: No. Every holding is cyclical: Tata Motors, Bajaj Finance, and HDFC Bank are early cyclicals, L&T is a late cyclical, and JSW Steel is a deep cyclical. They peak and trough at different times, but a real slowdown will hurt all of them. Worse, Karan's salary and job security depend on commercial vehicle demand, which is itself cyclical. In a downturn his portfolio and his income could fall together. Adding quasi-defensive and true defensive holdings, directly or through a fund, would give him exposure that behaves differently when his job is most at risk.

points: Think of cyclicality as a spectrum with five positions: deep cyclical, early cyclical, late cyclical, quasi-defensive, and true defensive
Deep cyclicals are commodity price takers with heavy fixed costs, so profits can vanish at the trough
Early cyclicals respond first to rate cuts and credit growth; late cyclicals depend on capex and turn later
Quasi-defensives like IT, pharma, and telecom see growth slow in a downturn while profits usually hold
True defensives rely on everyday necessity demand or regulated returns
Group your fund's sector allocation by spectrum position, not by sector count, to see how cyclical it really is

body.text: The profit changes in the bar chart and the fund allocation are illustrative. Company placements reflect typical business characteristics and can change over time, as the next lessons explain. References to listed companies are for education only and are not recommendations.
